sources.title: FEMA P-234 · Preparing for the next flood
sources.finding: Move contents above the flood protection level and deploy prepared floodproofing. Two people take approximately one hour to fill and place 100 sandbags for a one-foot-high, twenty-foot-long wall. Partial or poorly placed barriers can fail.
sources.kind: Official operating guidance; labor reference, not a local outcome trial

sources.title: City of Issaquah · Adopt a Drain
sources.finding: The program requests a 15-minute maintenance visit for monitoring, clearing leaves/litter and reporting. This is a service budget, not a timed San Francisco production study.

sources.title: FEMA · Hurricane Michael retrofit performance
sources.locator: Chapter 5, Tom P. Haney Technical Center, printed p. 5-18
sources.finding: Shutters did not preserve the intended recovery-shelter function when other wind vulnerabilities caused major building damage. Protecting openings does not establish whole-building protection.

sources.title: FEMA · Building performance after Hurricane Andrew
sources.finding: Missing or improperly installed connections and bracing contributed to framing failure. This mechanism does not validate an arbitrary brace or apply automatically to a San Francisco high-rise.

operations.label: Clear one inlet surface and adjacent gutter
operations.output: One inlet surface and reachable gutter cleared of loose leaves/litter
operations.without: Existing surface debris stays in place, if present.
operations.with: Surface blockage is removed; no change is claimed to below-grate blockage, sewer capacity or coastal flooding.
operations.evidence: SF crews clear catch basins during storms; SFPUC specifies safe surface-clearing practice. No matched local study quantifies damage avoided per cleared inlet.
operations.time_basis: 10–15 minutes of work, anchored to an external 15-minute maintenance budget; 5–10 minutes for setup is a planning allowance. Crew travel is added separately.
conditions: Actual surface debris present; if already clear, benefit is zero
Safe dry sidewalk, no storm or ponding; do not lift grate
Map point matched to actual inlet

operations.label: Move or tie down up to 10 loose exterior items
operations.output: Up to 10 small, accessible loose items stored indoors or secured
operations.without: Accessible loose objects remain potential windborne debris, if present.
operations.with: Remove the addressed objects as loose-debris sources; do not claim a change to design wind or structural strength.
operations.evidence: The March 2023 SF glazing investigation identified debris impacts among failure mechanisms. It did not test a quantified tie-down treatment effect.
operations.time_basis: Bounded planning estimate for a small two-person ground/balcony task; not a measured work rate. No roof, facade access, heavy lifting or anchors installed. Setup and estimated crew travel are added separately.
conditions: Owner access and suitable storage or rated attachment points
Only light items reachable from a safe floor; no roof or facade work
Count and attachment method confirmed before work

operations.label: Close and latch up to 10 accessible windows
operations.output: Up to 10 functioning accessible windows closed and latched
operations.without: Any open or unlatched window stays open or unlatched.
operations.with: Close the addressed openings; no credit for impact resistance, repairs or whole-building collapse prevention.
operations.evidence: SF's glazing investigation supports correcting window hardware/condition issues; closing operable windows does not address damaged glass or roof failure.
operations.time_basis: Planning estimate for one accessible area; hardware repairs and searching a whole tower are excluded. Setup and estimated crew travel are added separately.
conditions: Owner access and operable hardware
Actual open/unlatched windows; already-secured windows yield no additional benefit
No replacement glazing or work at height

operations.label: Move up to 10 portable boxes above the protection level
operations.output: Up to 10 portable boxes moved to a preselected safe upper storage area
operations.without: Those items remain exposed at their original level, if water reaches them.
operations.with: Remove direct flood exposure for the relocated items only; water entry and structural risk are unchanged.
operations.evidence: FEMA P-234 recommends moving contents above the protection level. It gives no matched storm damage-reduction estimate for this site.
operations.time_basis: Planning range for a short, unobstructed internal move; no heavy equipment, electrical disconnection or unknown stair carry. Setup and estimated crew travel are added separately.
conditions: Owner selects actual vulnerable items and a suitable protection level
Dry, usable route and safe storage capacity
Small loads within crew handling limits

operations.label: Install one stored, pre-fitted doorway barrier
operations.output: One compatible doorway barrier installed to its existing design
operations.without: That doorway has no added barrier protection.
operations.with: Block the addressed entry path within the barrier's verified design limit; backflow, seepage and overtopping remain possible.
operations.evidence_grade: Storm evidence shows a limiting condition
operations.evidence: FEMA's Sandy investigation documented overtopped floodgates. A barrier can only receive conditional benefit within its assessed protection level; an arbitrary barrier is not credited.
operations.time_basis: Planning estimate for deployment of an already fitted system; manufacture, delivery and new anchoring are excluded. Setup and estimated crew travel are added separately.
conditions: Stored compatible barrier and manufacturer's deployment instructions
Owner-approved entry path, design level, backflow and escape route
No field-fabricated structural flood load assumption

operations.label: Fill and place a 100-bag barrier segment
operations.output: One complete 100-bag segment at the referenced one-foot by twenty-foot geometry
operations.without: No new barrier segment is built.
operations.with: A complete correctly sited segment can divert shallow flow; a partially finished wall receives no protective credit.
operations.evidence: FEMA P-234 gives a two-person, approximately one-hour labor reference and warns that undersized or poorly built barriers fail. This is not a promise of watertightness or local damage reduction.
operations.time_basis: 60-minute published labor reference plus a 30-minute contingency and 10–20-minute setup allowance. Stock collection/delivery is excluded. Setup and estimated crew travel are added separately.
conditions: 100 bags and fill already at the site; ten public sandbags do not meet this bill of materials
Siting, ends, seepage, design water level and drainage assessed
Complete the segment before exposure; incomplete wall is not counted

operations.label: Deploy one pump on an existing approved backup circuit
operations.output: One compatible pump connected, discharge secured and operational load test completed
operations.without: No added pumping capacity or backup-supported pump is deployed.
operations.with: Support the specified pump during a grid outage, if the complete backup chain and discharge work; do not prevent the grid outage.
operations.evidence_grade: Operational benefit observed in a real storm
operations.evidence: FEMA P-942 documents a Manhattan building where additional sump pumps were connected to emergency power before Sandy, water was controlled and generators stayed operational. Other facilities lost backup because supporting components flooded.
operations.time_basis: Planning range for an already compatible pump/circuit; generator procurement, new wiring and repairs are excluded. Site test establishes real readiness. Setup and estimated crew travel are added separately.
conditions: Qualified electrician, owner approval and compatible existing circuit
Pump duty, discharge, protected switching/fuel and backup capacity confirmed
No live or flooded electrical work; no new unapproved interconnection

operations.label: Prune one arborist-specified defect
operations.output: One assessed pruning job completed to the arborist's scope
operations.without: The assessed tree defect remains untreated.
operations.with: Address that tree's defect; no universal failure-probability reduction is assigned.
operations.evidence: After Hurricane Andrew, studied properly pruned broad-leaved trees had 73% survival versus 47% for unpruned trees. This observational association does not establish a causal or San Francisco treatment effect, or justify last-minute indiscriminate pruning.
operations.time_basis: Planning range for a defined small specialist job; major removals, utility isolation, access/lift delays and disposal haulage can exceed it. Setup and estimated crew travel are added separately.
conditions: Current arborist scope, tree ownership and permissions
Qualified crew, appropriate rigging and exclusion area
Utility clearance where applicable; no general-crew chainsaw work

operations.label: Install one engineer-designed support package
operations.output: One previously designed and approved local support package installed and inspected
operations.without: The identified structural defect has no added support.
operations.with: Address the specific designed load path only; no blanket claim about preventing whole-building collapse.
operations.evidence_grade: Failure mechanism only; local applicability absent
operations.evidence: Andrew investigations link connection/bracing deficiencies to failure in light wood frames; Sandy documents other failure mechanisms. The mapped SF buildings' structural systems and designs are not established.
operations.time_basis: Planning allowance after engineering, permits and fabrication. Design/procurement lead time is additional and cannot be assumed to fit. Setup and estimated crew travel are added separately.
conditions: Site-specific engineer design, structure type and defect recorded
Approved materials, permits, access and inspection
No generic brace selected from footprint or building height

operations.label: Remove light loose debris from one access segment
operations.output: One short access segment cleared of light, loose, nonhazardous debris
operations.without: Any existing loose obstruction stays in the approach.
operations.with: Remove that obstruction; no claim about trees still standing, future debris, traffic safety or alternate-route reliability.
operations.evidence: SF Public Works documented tree/debris road obstructions during the 2023 storms. The record does not quantify the safety benefit of this proposed clearance.
operations.time_basis: Planning range for a short light-debris task; downed trees, wires, traffic exposure and heavy equipment are excluded. Setup and estimated crew travel are added separately.
conditions: Current light obstruction and safe work area confirmed
No power-line contact, trees requiring cutting or hazardous waste
Authorized access maintained

operations.label: Place one authorized closure with signed alternate access
operations.output: One approved closure and signed, checked alternative in place
operations.without: No new restriction or alternate-route signs are installed.
operations.with: Reduce access to the identified danger area; do not count this as less physical storm damage.
operations.evidence: San Francisco's storm annex assigns closure and access control to the responsible agencies. It does not measure avoided injuries for this location.
operations.time_basis: Planning range after a route/control plan and authority approval; design and approval time are excluded. Setup and estimated crew travel are added separately.
conditions: Traffic authority approval and actual hazard trigger
Verified alternative preserves emergency and accessible travel
Qualified traffic crew and approved signs/barriers
